item.text:
**Bottom line:** yes, Biden’s 2024 governing ideology was clear enough to evaluate later action against. The core program was consistent across his SOTU, budget, and party materials: middle-out economics, lower costs, expanded social benefits, pro-union/pro-consumer policy, and a democracy-vs-autocracy frame. The main weakness is that, after the debate collapse and withdrawal, the reelection effort became more defensive and anti-Trump/Project 2025-centered than a stable second-term blueprint.

| Evidence | Why it matters for `8B.1` | IDs |
|---|---|---|
| [Address Before a Joint Session of the Congress on the State of the Union](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/address-before-joint-session-the-congress-the-state-the-union-30) - The American Presidency Project, 2024-03-07 | Biden explicitly laid out a governing frame: freedom and democracy under assault, “middle out and bottom up” growth, a “fair shot,” no one left behind, and restoration of Roe. That is a clear ideology/program, not just ad hoc rhetoric. | `8B.1` |
| [FACT SHEET: The President's Budget Lowers Costs for the American People](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/fact-sheet-the-presidents-budget-lowers-costs-for-the-american-people) - The American Presidency Project, 2024-03-11 | The budget translates the ideology into a policy agenda: lower costs, treat health care as a right, expand child care, housing, college access, broadband, and make wealthy corporations pay their fair share. This is a concrete second-term program. | `8B.1` |
| [Remarks by National Economic Advisor Lael Brainard on Lowering Costs for American Consumers](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-national-economic-advisor-lael-brainard-lowering-costs-for-american-consumers) - The American Presidency Project, 2024-06-20 | Biden’s top domestic priority is stated plainly as lowering costs for middle-class families, using government tools to cut prices in essential household categories. That is strategic direction that can be checked against later policy. | `8B.1` |
| [Memorial Day remarks: “Every generation has to earn it”](https://www.ap.org/news-highlights/elections/2024/biden-says-each-generation-has-to-earn-freedom-in-solemn-memorial-day-remarks/) - Associated Press, 2024-05-27 | Biden described the governing moral conflict as “autocracy vs democracy” and “the greed of a few” vs “the rights of many,” then tied that to freedom, opportunity, and equality. This is a highly legible governing ideology. | `8B.1` |
| [2024 Democratic Party Platform](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/2024-democratic-party-platform) - The American Presidency Project, 2024-08-18 | The platform shows continuity around Biden’s agenda after he stepped aside: protect Social Security/Medicare, keep Medicare drug-price reforms, oppose special-interest giveaways, and advance middle-class relief. It is useful as the revealed governing program attached to his coalition. | `8B.1` |
| [How Project 2025’s rightward vision became a flashpoint in this year’s election](https://www.ap.org/news-highlights/elections/2024/how-project-2025s-rightward-vision-became-a-flashpoint-in-this-years-election/) - Associated Press, 2024-08-21 | Biden’s campaign used Project 2025 as a shorthand warning about Trump’s second term, which reveals a clear strategic goal: frame the election as a defense of democracy against an authoritarian/right-wing program. That is explicit, but it is also more oppositional than a full positive governing blueprint. | `8B.1` |
| [Biden drops out of 2024 race after disastrous debate inflamed age concerns. VP Harris gets his nod](https://www.ap.org/news-highlights/elections/2024/biden-drops-out-of-2024-race-after-disastrous-debate-inflamed-age-concerns-vp-harris-gets-his-nod/) - Associated Press, 2024-07-21 | The reelection effort lost coherence after the debate; Biden said he would finish the term, then stepped aside and endorsed Harris, with Democrats suddenly needing to “bring coherence” to the nomination fight. This weakens the case for a stable, fully articulated second-term governing program in the back half of 2024. | `8B.1`, `7B.8` |

Search gap: I did not find a single 2024 document that reads like a standalone second-term manifesto for Biden. The ideology is clear in fragments and budgetary priorities, but once the campaign crisis hit, the public-facing strategic direction shifted toward anti-Trump/Project 2025 defense and managed transition rather than a clean, intact governing blueprint.
